title: Express conditions to performance
summary: An express condition is an event the parties specify must occur before a duty becomes due, or whose occurrence affects that duty as the agreement provides.
notes:
Luttinger’s financing condition made the buyers’ duty depend on obtaining a qualifying mortgage after the required effort. Gibson’s satisfaction condition concerned the buyer’s judgment of a portrait. Peacock asks whether a clause tied payment to an event as a true risk-shifting condition or merely fixed payment timing. The wording and transaction determine the difference.

A condition is distinct from a promise. Failure of a condition may mean that a duty never becomes due without itself being a breach. A person can also promise to bring about the condition, in which case failure may have both effects. Interpretation, excuse, waiver, and prevention must be analyzed before concluding that nonoccurrence defeats recovery.
